# TryIPTV — Site Context

## About TryIPTV

TryIPTV is a prepaid IPTV subscription service at https://www.tryiptv.com/. Brand name: TryIPTV (logo wordmark: "Try IPTV"). Tagline: "Prepaid IPTV with a 24-hour free trial". TryIPTV sells its own subscriptions and issues the login details itself. Viewers use those details in compatible third-party IPTV player applications. TryIPTV does not develop or own the player apps described on its website.

The website separates five intents: commercial pages describe the service and terms; device pages explain platform setup; player pages explain specific apps; guides explain IPTV concepts; help pages diagnose symptoms. Each question is answered most fully on the most specific page.

## Company

- Operated by: Simo Alaoui LLC, New York, United States
- Company registration number: 8683949 (New York Department of State)
- Operating since: 2021
- Founder / Operations: Simo Alaoui, who oversees TryIPTV's operations, customer experience and service development
- Support: WhatsApp wa.me/tryiptvcom and support@tryiptv.com, 9:00 AM–10:00 PM ET, every day including weekends and public holidays; replies typically within 15 minutes during those hours, and messages sent outside them are answered when support reopens
- Press and media: press@tryiptv.com (media contact: Simo Alaoui, Founder / Operations)
- About page: https://www.tryiptv.com/about

## Service facts

- Service model: fixed-term prepaid plans with no automatic renewal.
- Access methods: M3U playlist URLs and Xtream Codes-style credentials.
- Simultaneous connections: two active streams under a standard plan.
- Typical credential delivery and activation: 5–15 minutes after confirmation; this is not an instant guarantee.
- The catalog is 25,000+ live channels worldwide and 120,000+ movies and TV shows, counted from TryIPTV's channel and on-demand lists in October 2026. Availability and playback quality may vary.

The [FAQ](https://www.tryiptv.com/faq) answers common service questions. The [homepage](https://www.tryiptv.com/) provides the service overview.

[Pricing](https://www.tryiptv.com/pricing) is the authority for current prices and plan inclusions.

## Trial and refunds

The [free trial page](https://www.tryiptv.com/iptv-free-trial) describes a 24-hour trial that costs $0 and requires no credit card. The trial includes two simultaneous connections, the same as paid plans. That page holds the current request process and trial conditions.

The [refund policy](https://www.tryiptv.com/refund-policy) states that once a subscription is activated and account details are delivered, all sales are final. A refund is only issued when TryIPTV cannot provide a working subscription (for example, the account is not delivered or the service does not start at all). Refunds are not given for internet issues, device or player incompatibility, or channel changes. Refund requests are answered within 24–48 hours.

The [terms and conditions](https://www.tryiptv.com/terms-conditions), [privacy policy](https://www.tryiptv.com/privacy-policy), and [disclaimer](https://www.tryiptv.com/disclaimer) provide further policy detail.

## Setup and devices

The [setup overview](https://www.tryiptv.com/setup) explains the general path: receive credentials, choose a compatible player, enter the supplied connection details, and test playback. The [devices hub](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices) directs readers to platform-specific instructions. Device guides cover:

- [Fire TV Stick](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/firestick-iptv)
- [Android TV and Google TV](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/android-tv-iptv)
- [Samsung TV](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/samsung-tv-iptv)
- [LG TV](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/lg-tv-iptv)
- [Apple TV](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/apple-tv-iptv)
- [iPhone and iPad](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/iphone-iptv)
- [Chromecast](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/chromecast-iptv)
- [MAG Box](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/mag-box-iptv)
- [Roku](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/roku-iptv)
- [Windows](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/windows-iptv)
- [macOS](https://www.tryiptv.com/devices/mac-iptv)

Device guides own the steps for their named platform. Check the relevant guide for player availability and setup methods; availability can vary by device and region.

## IPTV concepts

The [guides hub](https://www.tryiptv.com/guides) collects explanatory articles:

- [What is IPTV?](https://www.tryiptv.com/guides/what-is-iptv) defines internet-delivered television; [how IPTV works](https://www.tryiptv.com/guides/how-does-iptv-work) explains the delivery process.
- [M3U](https://www.tryiptv.com/guides/what-is-m3u) is a playlist format listing media locations and related metadata.
- [Xtream Codes](https://www.tryiptv.com/guides/what-are-xtream-codes) describes a structured login/API convention using a server URL, username, and password.
- [M3U vs Xtream Codes](https://www.tryiptv.com/guides/m3u-vs-xtream-codes) compares the two connection methods; it is distinct from their definitions.
- [EPG](https://www.tryiptv.com/guides/what-is-epg) is the user-facing electronic programme guide containing channel schedule information. XMLTV is one structured format used to carry schedule data; the terms are not interchangeable.
- [Internet speed](https://www.tryiptv.com/guides/iptv-internet-speed) explains bandwidth and connection stability. [IPTV vs cable](https://www.tryiptv.com/guides/iptv-vs-cable) compares delivery models.

## Troubleshooting

The [help hub](https://www.tryiptv.com/help) directs readers by symptom. The [general IPTV not working checklist](https://www.tryiptv.com/help/iptv-not-working) helps identify the failing layer before following a specific diagnostic page:

- [Login not working](https://www.tryiptv.com/help/iptv-login-not-working): credentials, login method, and server reachability.
- [M3U not loading](https://www.tryiptv.com/help/m3u-not-loading): playlist URL, download, and parsing problems.
- [EPG not working](https://www.tryiptv.com/help/epg-not-working): missing, stale, or incorrect programme data when channels may still play.
- [IPTV buffering](https://www.tryiptv.com/help/iptv-buffering): interrupted playback and connection or player factors.

Troubleshooting depends on the observed symptom. The site does not guarantee buffering-free playback or universal 4K availability.
